M5 Smart vs M9: Which Pump Is Right for You?
Shelly Umstot is a BSN and has been a registered nurse for over 35 years. She lives in North East Ohio and is a freelance health content writer. Her passion is bringing understanding to those with questions and concerns regarding health issues and helping them obtain and maintain their optimal health. She loves being with her family and has two lovely granddaughters who have stolen her heart. Assisting new parents in finding the information they need to face the joys and challenges of caring for their children is a gratifying experience for her as a professional, parent, and grandparent herself.
Comparing the Momcozy M5 Smart vs M9 is one of the most common questions new and returning pumping moms ask. Both pumps are hands-free, app-connected, and built for real life on the go. But they come with meaningful differences in motor power, pumping modes, design, and price. This guide walks through every key detail so you can pick the pump that truly works for you .

Both the M5 Smart and the M9 connect to the Momcozy app via Bluetooth. That means you can adjust settings from your phone instead of reaching into your bra during a meeting or a commute. However, what you can do inside the app differs quite a bit between the two models.
M5 Smart Wearable Breast Pump – Upgraded with App Control
Momcozy Mobile Flow™ Hands-Free Breast Pump | M9
The M5 Smart is the upgraded version of the classic M5 , Amazon's best-selling breast pump . The biggest change is the addition of app connectivity. Once you pair it with the Momcozy app (compatible with iOS 13 and Android 8.0 or higher), you can start or stop sessions, switch pumping modes, and adjust suction levels right from your screen. The app also lets you log each session with time, duration, and milk volume, then view daily, weekly, and monthly summaries. You can track trends over time and share data with a lactation consultant if needed. The pump still works with the physical buttons too, so the app is optional rather than required.
The M9 goes further. Beyond the same remote controls and session logging you get with the M5 Smart, the M9 app unlocks two professional pumping modes that are not available on the M5 Smart at all. Milk Boost™ helps moms who want to build or increase their milk supply. Milk Relief™ gently eases discomfort and encourages milk flow for moms experiencing engorgement. The app also offers MyFlow™ Mode, which lets you create a fully personalized pumping pattern by adjusting the mode type and intensity to match exactly what feels right for your body. The M9 also has a left/right toggle button on the pump itself so you can easily track which side you are pumping.
The M5 Smart has a classic semi-circular shape that curves naturally against the breast. It measures 5.0 in x 4.6 in x 2.9 in (128 mm x 117 mm x 74 mm). The M9 uses a tear-drop design intended to more closely follow the natural shape of the breast, making it sit a little more discreetly under clothing. It measures 5.0 in x 4.3 in x 3.0 in (127 mm x 109 mm x 77 mm).
One practical advantage of the M9 design is its flat base.

You can set the M9 down on any flat surface without it tipping over, even when it is full of milk. The M5 Smart has a rounded base, so if you remove it while it still contains milk, you will need to transfer the milk right away or hold it upright to prevent spills.
Both pumps come in 2 color options: Cozy Red and Quill Grey. Both include 5 main parts, one USB-C charging cable, and one flange cover.
Both the M5 Smart and M9 feature the DoubleFit flange with a 105-degree slope. This angle mimics the natural curvature of a baby's mouth during nursing, which helps reduce compression on milk ducts and supports more comfortable, efficient pumping. Tests show this design improves pumping efficiency by 28.2% and reduces leakage by 10%.
The flange materials do differ. The M5 Smart uses soft silicone throughout, which creates a gentle, flexible feel against the breast. The M9 uses a combination of hard and soft silicone: the inner surface that touches your breast is soft, while the section that connects to the milk bowl is firm to create a better seal and prevent leaks.
Both pumps include a standard 24 mm flange plus three flange inserts: 17 mm, 19 mm, and 21 mm. If you have larger nipples, both models are also compatible with a 27 mm flange, sold separately.
The M5 Smart milk collector holds 5.4 oz (160 ml) and has a rounded bottom. It does not include a lid. After each session, you need to transfer the milk into a storage bag or bottle right away.
The M9 milk collector holds 5.1 oz (150 ml) and has a flat base so it stands upright on its own. It comes with a lid, which means once you finish pumping, you can snap the lid on and place the collector directly in the refrigerator without transferring the milk first. This is especially convenient when you are pumping on the go or in the middle of a busy workday.
Both collectors use BPA-free materials. The M9 uses Tritan, a medical-grade copolyester known for being highly durable, resistant to odors and stains, and able to withstand over 100 boiling cycles without deforming.
For both pumps, stop pumping before the milk reaches the 4.2 oz (120 ml) mark to prevent overflow.
The M5 Smart has a clear LED screen that shows the current pumping mode and suction level. Battery life appears briefly when you first power the pump on.
The M9 has a larger, clearer LED screen that displays the same basics plus a built-in timer so you can see exactly how long you have been pumping. The M9 screen also shows continuous battery life during use. In addition, the M9 has a dedicated left/right toggle button on the unit so you can switch between tracking your left and right breast sessions easily.
This is one of the most significant differences between these two pumps. The M5 Smart uses Momcozy's 1st generation motor. The M9 uses the 3rd generation motor, which is more powerful and operates more quietly. The upgraded motor is what makes the M9's extra suction levels and advanced modes possible.
The M5 Smart offers 9 suction levels and reaches a maximum suction of 285 mmHg . The M9 offers 15 suction levels and reaches a maximum of 300 mmHg . Having more levels means the M9 lets you make finer adjustments. The jump between each level feels smaller, so you can dial in exactly the right pressure for your comfort. Independent left/right suction control is available on the M9, while the M5 Smart adjusts both sides at the same time.
Both pumps include three standard pumping modes. Stimulation mode uses a quick, short sucking pattern to trigger your letdown reflex, similar to how a baby first latches. Expression mode switches to a slower, deeper sucking pattern to draw out milk efficiently. Mixed mode starts with the quick stimulation pattern and then transitions into the slower expression pattern, working through both phases automatically.
The M9 adds three more options available through the app. Milk Boost is designed to help moms increase their milk supply by mimicking power pumping. Milk Relief uses a balanced, quic

k-release flow to ease engorgement gently. MyFlow Mode lets you build a completely custom pattern by choosing the base mode and setting your own intensity. None of these three modes are available on the M5 Smart.
Stimulation mode : -75 to -145 (plus or minus 30) mmHg, 50-120 cycles per minute
Expression mode : -120 to -285 (plus or minus 30) mmHg, 23-57 cycles per minute
Mixed mode : -75 to -285 (plus or minus 30) mmHg, 6-16 cycles per minute
Stimulation mode : -67 to -172 mmHg, 62-90 cycles per minute
Expression mode : -105 to -300 mmHg, 26-60 cycles per minute
Mixed mode : -105 to -300 mmHg, 50-85 cycles per minute
Both pumps deliver roughly the same amount of pumping time on a full charge. After a complete charge, each model supports 4 to 5 pumping sessions of about 30 minutes each, totaling approximately 150 minutes of use. That is enough to get most moms through a full workday before needing to plug in again.
The difference is in how long they take to recharge. The M5 Smart reaches a full charge in about 120 minutes. The M9 takes around 150 minutes to fully charge. Both pumps use a USB Type-C cable, and neither can be used while it is charging.
One extra feature on the M9 is a built-in dust plug for the USB-C charging port. This protects the port from lint, dust, and moisture over time, which can help extend the life of the charging connection. The M5 Smart does not include this protective cap.
For long-term care, both pumps have a rechargeable lithium-ion battery with a product use life of 500 hours. If you store either pump for an extended period, charge it every three months to keep the battery healthy.
Both pumps are cord-free and fully wearable inside a nursing bra, which is the whole point of a wearable pump. You can move around, work, cook, or run errands while you pump. Both models come with a carrying case to keep all the parts organized when you head out.
The M5 Smart weighs 8.1 oz (230 g). The M9 weighs 10.7 oz (302 g). The difference is noticeable if you are sensitive to weight in your bra during longer sessions. If you are looking for the lightest option, the M5 Smart wins here.
Both pumps run quietly enough for office use. The M5 Smart operates at 50 dB or below, which is about as loud as a quiet library. The M9 runs at 42 dB or below, making it slightly quieter. Both levels are discreet enough for most environments, including meetings and public spaces.
Keeping your pump clean protects your baby from germs that can grow quickly in breast milk residue. Fortunately, both the M5 Smart and M9 are designed to make cleaning as simple as possible.
Both pumps have 4 milk-contact parts to clean after every use: the flange, diaphragm, valve, and milk collector. (The M9 milk collector lid also needs to be washed if you use it.) The motor unit on both pumps never touches breast milk and should never be submerged in water. Wipe it down with a clean soft cloth or 70% isopropyl alcohol wipe instead.
The cleaning process is the same for both models. After each use, rinse the milk-contact parts under running water, then wash them in a clean basin using warm water (104-140 degrees F / 40-60 degrees C) and soap. Scrub with a brush reserved for baby items, rinse thoroughly, and air dry on a clean towel. Do not use a dishwasher, microwave, or UV sterilizer for either pump. Do not use antibacterial or abrasive cleaning agents, as these can damage the silicone parts.
For disinfection, which is especially important if your baby is under 3 months, premature, or has a weakened immune system, boil the disassembled milk-contact parts in water for about 3 to 5 minutes. Make sure the parts do not touch the sides of the pot. Remove them with clean tongs and air dry completely before reassembling.
Silicone valves and diaphragms on both models typically last one to three months with regular use. Check them regularly for cracks, tears, or discoloration and replace them when needed to maintain good suction.
Both pumps take less than 30 secon

ds to assemble once you know the steps. Always wash your hands before touching any pump parts, and make sure all parts have cooled completely if you just disinfected them with boiling water.
Attach the diaphragm to the milk collector, pressing gently around the edges until it seals.
Gently push the valve into the flange with no gaps.
Align the flange with the milk collector so the patterns overlap, then press down firmly with your thumbs around the rim.
Attach the pump motor to the milk collector assembly.
Rotate the milk bowl in the direction of the lock icon at the mouth of the bottle.
Fasten the flange to the mouth of the bottle and connect it with the milk collector.
Connect the main unit to the assembled flange.
The M5 Smart (double pump) is priced at $199.99 . The M9 (double pump) is priced at $269.99 , which is $70 more. Both pumps are also available as single pump options.
The $70 difference reflects the M9's 3rd generation motor, 15 suction levels, higher max suction, additional professional app modes, quieter operation, flat-base milk collector with lid, and charging port dust plug. Both pumps include a carrying case and a one-year warranty.
You want app control and session tracking at an accessible price ($199.99)
You are new to pumping and want a simple, reliable pump without too many options to navigate
You pump occasionally rather than throughout the entire day
You prefer a lighter pump at 8.1 oz (230 g) for longer wear comfort
You have a consistent milk supply and do not need specialized milk-production modes
You want a pump that is easy to set up and use right out of the box
You pump frequently or exclusively and need every tool available to support your supply
You want Milk Boost™, Milk Relief™, or MyFlow™ personalized pattern control
You need to adjust each side of your pump independently
You want the convenience of a flat-base milk collector with a lid for fridge storage
You pump in public or at work and want the quietest possible operation
You are an experienced pumper upgrading and want more precision and control
M5 Smart vs M9: Which Pump Is Right for You ?
Both the Momcozy M5 Smart and M9 are excellent wearable breast pumps that give you the freedom to keep moving while you pump. The M5 Smart delivers reliable app-connected performance in a lightweight, easy-to-use package. The M9 steps up with a more powerful motor, greater suction control, professional modes, and the added convenience of a lidded milk collecto r. Match the features to your actual pumping routine, and either pump will support your breastfeeding journey with confidence.
